summary: This Wikipedia-derived note surveys the Late Middle Ages across Europe, covering the Scandinavian Kalmar Union and Sweden's break from Denmark, cultural and scientific progress including the Italian Renaissance, and the Ottoman advance into Southeastern Europe. It also covers Hungary's defense under John Hunyadi, Bohemia and the Holy Roman Empire, changes in music and army recruitment, the 'commercial revolution' in finance, and the decline of Bulgaria and Serbia in the Balkans.
one_line: Overview of Late Middle Ages Europe: Scandinavian unions, Renaissance beginnings, music, armies, commerce, and Ottoman conquest of the Balkans.
key_facts: The Kalmar Union was instituted in 1397 as a pan-Scandinavian union dominated by Denmark.
King Christian II of Denmark had large numbers of the Swedish aristocracy killed in the Stockholm Bloodbath of 1520.
Sweden broke away for good from the Kalmar Union in 1523.
Norway remained united with Denmark until 1814.
The capture of Constantinople by the Ottoman Turks accelerated the availability of Greek texts in the West as Byzantine scholars sought refuge in Italy.
After King Vladislaus I of Hungary died at the Battle of Varna in 1444, John Hunyadi became Hungary's regent-governor (1446–1453).
Pope Pius II awarded John Hunyadi the title Athleta Christi, or Champion of Christ.
The Golden Bull of 1356 made the king of Bohemia first among the imperial electors.
The Holy Roman Empire passed to the Habsburgs in 1438 and remained with them until its dissolution in 1806.
Guillaume de Machaut and Philippe de Vitry were the main representatives of the ars nova style.
John Kukuzelis was a prominent reformer of Orthodox Church music in the first half of the 14th century and introduced a notation system widely used in the Balkans.
The Serbian army led by Lazar Hrebljevanovic was defeated by the Ottomans at the Battle of Kosovo in 1389.
Serbian victory over the Bulgarians at the Battle of Velbazhd in 1330 marked Serbia's ascendancy.
Belgrade, a Hungarian domain at the time, was the last large Balkan city to fall under Ottoman rule, in 1521.
Historians term the late 13th and early 14th century process a 'commercial revolution', including double-entry bookkeeping and the bill of exchange.
